result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.lukes_partitioning()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Optimally partition a tree into clusters of bounded size (Lukes' algorithm). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26503-L26578){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.lukes_partitioning( max_size, node_weight=None, edge_weight=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Lukes partitioning](/assets/graphs/lukes-partitioning.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A path of six nodes, A to F, cut into connected clusters of at most three nodes. The best split cuts only the middle edge C to D (dashed), keeping 4 of the 5 edges inside clusters: A, B, C in the accent color and D, E, F in teal, as the card lists." width="100%"} Cuts a tree into connected clusters whose total node weight is at most `max_size`, keeping as much edge weight inside clusters as possible (equivalently, cutting the lightest possible set of edges). It solves bounded-size clustering exactly on trees, as when grouping the branches of a distribution network into service areas, packing a hierarchy into pages or memory blocks, or splitting a phylogeny into balanced clades. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The maximum total node weight of a cluster. [node_weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute with non-negative integer weights (default: every node weighs 1). [edge_weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute with the value of keeping an edge inside a cluster (default: every edge is worth 1). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The clusters as sets of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not a tree, a node weight is not a non-negative integer, or a single node weighs more than `max_size`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Lukes (1974) is a dynamic program over the tree: for each subtree and each possible weight of the cluster containing its root, the best kept edge weight, combined child by child either by cutting the edge to the child or by merging the child's root cluster. It runs in $O(n K^2)$ time for `max_size` $K$ and finds an optimum; the kept weight matches NetworkX's `lukes_partitioning` (which may return a different optimal partition). Edge direction is ignored. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path of six nodes cut into pieces of at most three nodes keeps four of its five edges when cut in the middle: ::: {#62309e27 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEF")) path.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F")]) [sorted(path.get_label_from_id(n) for n in c) for c in path.lukes_partitioning(3)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [['A', 'B', 'C'], ['D', 'E', 'F']] ``` ::: :::
